answer: Moving a session to a new device requires signatures from both the old device and the new device on the same migration request. An attacker holding only the new device cannot complete the move, and an attacker holding only the old device cannot redirect the session to a device it controls, so both halves must be genuinely owned. Auditors look for the voyage that does not belong: a recovery with no valid proof attached. When the timber settles over the signal, the account stands because every recovery carried its own proof.
